name: TLN Protocol spot-reserve reward and collateral manipulation
summary: TLNProtocolStaking priced staked VOW/vUSD LP from live reserves of that pool and the thin VOW/USDT pair, and TlnSwap.lock sized VOW collateral from the same live reserves. A flash-loaned VOW buy let the attacker stake a little LP for millions of TLN, lock it for vUSD against negligible VOW, and sell the vUSD through VOW for USDT.
notes: Both contracts are non-proxies whose constructors fixed the reserve-reading pairs; later governance calls only changed staking eligibility, so each ages from deployment.

vUSD and VOW had no market that could absorb the anchor's take, so the anchor is valued at what the attacker realised: its USDT and 3,280 VOW sold for BNB, and 1,460,000 VOW bridged to Ethereum and sold for ETH (rule 12).

Ten copycat flash-loan transactions repeated the stake-and-dump a week later (via a newly deployed swap contract); their loss is the USDT they drained from the VOW/USDT pair, found by its flash-sized round-trip swaps through the latest block.
